units: points; page and top/left/baseline measured from the page top-left corner; start/end are UTF-16 offsets in the main story
precision: top/left/lastX are screen-quantised (+-0.3 pt); baseline/inkLeft and cell rectangles come from the 600 dpi PDF and are exact

lines.text: The morning ferry crosses the estuary twice before the tide turns, carrying commuters, bicycles and
crates of vegetables from the farms on the far shore. Nobody on board hurries; they read, drink tea from
flasks and watch the herons stand in the shallows. When the ferry docks, a short queue forms along the
jetty and the deckhand coils the rope with practised ease.
A well-made map leaves out far more than it shows. The cartographer decides which roads matter, which
rivers deserve a name and where a label may sit without hiding a village. Every choice trades detail for
clarity, and the reader trusts the result because the trades were made carefully and applied the same
way across the whole sheet.
In the workshop the lamps stay lit late. Shavings gather under the bench, a kettle ticks as it cools, and the
half-finished chair waits for its last joint. The maker steps back, squints along the rail and decides that
tomorrow will do for the glue, since good work is not improved by being rushed past the point of care.
